title: HTTP Request Smuggling: CL.TE Dual Header Desync
attack_vector: Front-end uses Content-Length header, back-end uses Transfer-Encoding: chunked. Trailing request bytes poison backend connection pool.
impact: Unauthenticated cache poisoning, credential theft via request hijacking, complete authentication bypass.
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: HTTP Desync Attacks (James Kettle, DEF CON 27)
remediation: Disable connection reuse on backend, normalize HTTP requests at reverse proxy, enforce HTTP/2 end-to-end.

title: HTTP Request Smuggling: TE.CL Desync via Obfuscated Transfer-Encoding
attack_vector: Front-end uses Transfer-Encoding, back-end uses Content-Length. Obfuscated TE header (e.g., Transfer-Encoding: xchunked or double TE) causes back-end to fall back to Content-Length.
impact: Session hijacking, redirect hijacking, internal admin endpoint access.
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: HTTP Request Smuggling (James Kettle)
remediation: Reject ambiguous requests containing both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers (RFC 7230 §3.3.3).

title: HTTP/2 Request Smuggling: H2.TE Request Splitting (Downgrade Flaw)
attack_vector: Front-end speaks HTTP/2 to client but downgrades to HTTP/1.1 to upstream backend. Attacker injects Transfer-Encoding in pseudo-headers or binary framing.
detection_probe: H2 request with header 'transfer-encoding: chunked' and message body desynchronizing HTTP/1.1 backend.
impact: Account takeover via stolen ambient session tokens, request queuing delay attacks.
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: HTTP/2: The Sequel is Always Worse (James Kettle, Black Hat 2021)
remediation: Enforce HTTP/2 end-to-end to back-end services; strip pseudo-headers and sanitize headers during protocol translation.

title: Web Cache Poisoning via Unkeyed Host & Header Reflection
attack_vector: Reverse proxy cache hashes URL path but excludes headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Host, X-Forwarded-Scheme). Application reflects unkeyed header into script src imports.
impact: Stored cross-site scripting served to every subsequent visitor of the cached resource.
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: Practical Web Cache Poisoning (James Kettle, Black Hat 2018)
remediation: Include all request headers that alter response content in the cache key, or disable unkeyed header handling.

title: Web Cache Poisoning: Fat GET Request Parameter Cloaking
attack_vector: Front-end cache ignores request body for GET requests, but back-end web framework (e.g. Ruby on Rails, Node.js) parses query parameters from both URL and body, prioritizing body.
impact: Arbitrary JavaScript execution delivered from legitimate CDN edge node.
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: Web Cache Entanglement (James Kettle, Black Hat 2020)
remediation: Configure reverse proxy caches to reject GET requests with non-empty message bodies (Content-Length > 0).

title: Web Cache Deception via Path Delimiter Confusion
attack_vector: Web server strips trailing non-existent path extension (e.g. /account/settings/test.css) and returns authenticated HTML, while caching proxy caches based on .css static extension.
impact: Sensitive user profile, API keys, CSRF tokens, and PII cached on public CDN and readable by unauthenticated attackers.
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: Web Cache Deception (Omer Gil / James Kettle)
remediation: Set Cache-Control: no-store, private on dynamic endpoints; configure cache to only cache static responses based on Content-Type header.

title: Client-Side Prototype Pollution via Query & Hash Parameters
attack_vector: Client-side JavaScript recursive object merge / deep clone copies user-controlled URL properties into Object.prototype, altering global property lookups.
impact: DOM XSS via gadget chains in popular frontend libraries (lodash, jQuery, Google Analytics, sanitize-html).
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: Client-side prototype pollution (Gareth Heyes, Black Hat 2021)
remediation: Use Object.create(null) for dictionaries, freeze Object.prototype with Object.freeze(), or sanitize object keys.

title: Server-Side Prototype Pollution: Remote Code Execution in Node.js
attack_vector: Backend JSON deserialization and deep-merge mutates global Object.prototype in Node.js runtime, polluting child_process.execFile options (e.g., shell, env, NODE_OPTIONS).
impact: Full Remote Code Execution on Node.js application servers.
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: Server-side prototype pollution (Mikhail Shcherbakov, Gareth Heyes)
remediation: Validate JSON schemas strictly; prohibit '__proto__' and 'constructor' keys in JSON parsers; run node with --disable-proto=delete.

title: OAuth 2.0 Account Hijacking via redirect_uri Path Traversal
attack_vector: Authorization server validates redirect_uri domain with prefix/regex matching. Attacker uses path traversal or open redirect parameter on whitelist domain to leak authorization codes.
impact: Complete account takeover without user password.
author_reference: PortSwigger Web Security Academy: OAuth 2.0 Authentication Vulnerabilities
remediation: Require strict exact string match for redirect_uri against pre-registered client callbacks.

title: JWT Signature Bypass via Algorithm Confusion (RS256 to HS256)
attack_vector: Server expects RS256 token signed with private RSA key. Attacker changes token header to 'alg': 'HS256' and signs token using server's public RSA key (which is public knowledge).
detection_probe: JWT header: {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"} signed with RSA public key as HMAC secret.
impact: Arbitrary user impersonation including administrative privilege escalation.
author_reference: PortSwigger Web Security Academy: JWT Attacks
remediation: Explicitly enforce expected signing algorithm on the server; never trust header 'alg' parameter blindly.

title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in Modern Web Engines
attack_vector: Unsanitized user input is concatenated directly into template source string instead of being passed as context parameter, executing template expressions.
impact: Remote code execution, file disclosure, environment credential theft across Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, Thymeleaf, SpEL.
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: Server-Side Template Injection (James Kettle, Black Hat 2015)
remediation: Never concatenate user input directly into template strings; use parameterized template context.

title: GraphQL Mutation Batching & Introspection Information Leak
attack_vector: Production GraphQL schema enables __schema introspection and permits batch array requests in single POST, bypassing rate limiting and discovering unauthenticated mutations.
impact: Full API schema exposure, credential brute-forcing via batched queries, privilege escalation.
author_reference: PortSwigger Web Security Academy: GraphQL Vulnerabilities
remediation: Disable introspection in production; implement query depth and complexity limits; enforce per-operation rate limits.

title: SSRF Cloud Metadata Exfiltration (AWS / GCP / Azure)
attack_vector: Server fetches external URL provided by user (webhooks, avatar imports, PDF generators) without IP sanitization, reaching link-local instance metadata service.
impact: Temporary AWS IAM role keys, GCP service account tokens, full cloud infrastructure compromise.
author_reference: PortSwigger Web Security Academy: Server-Side Request Forgery
remediation: Enforce IMDSv2 (token-based session headers); filter non-routable IPv4/IPv6 private ranges in application firewall.

title: Single-Packet Race Condition: Multi-Endpoint Limit Overrun
attack_vector: Synchronized HTTP/2 single-packet requests exploit time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) windows in checkout, voucher redemption, or funds transfer.
detection_probe: Concurrent requests aligned using HTTP/2 multiplexing or TCP packet buffering to arrive within sub-millisecond window.
impact: Gift card double-spending, coupon reuse, vote manipulation, balance duplication.
author_reference: PortSwigger Research: Smashing the state machine: the true potential of web race conditions (James Kettle, Black Hat 2023)
remediation: Use database row-level locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) or atomic transactions with idempotency keys.
